scenes.narration: Hugging Face's Microduck is a 25-centimetre walking robot, under 800 grams. Its CEO says it's heading for about 20,000 preorders.
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real close-up of a small bipedal hobby robot standing on a wooden desk next to a ruler, shallow depth of field, workshop lighting
scenes.speaker: Meera

scenes.narration: Fifteen motors, a camera, a depth sensor, and a beak that lifts about 100 grams. It walks, crouches, gets up after falls, and can even roller-skate.
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real macro shot of small servo motors and wiring inside a hobby robot on a workbench, soft overhead light
scenes.speaker: Arjun

scenes.narration: So how? Reinforcement learning in a physics simulator. Fall, retry, improve. Then the skill transfers to the real robot. That's sim-to-real.
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real over-the-shoulder shot of a laptop screen showing an illustrative physics simulation of a walking robot figure, dim office
scenes.speaker: Meera

scenes.narration: At Nvidia GTC Berlin, four were demoed live. They stumbled and wandered. Real floors are hard.
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real wide shot of a tech conference stage with small robots on a floor and an audience watching, event lighting
scenes.speaker: Arjun

scenes.narration: The software is open source. The hardware designs aren't, according to Pollen.
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real close-up of hands typing code on a laptop beside a robot chassis on a desk, warm light
scenes.speaker: Meera

scenes.narration: $399 before tax and shipping. New orders: about four to six months. A developer platform, not a toy.
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real shot of a laptop showing a generic online checkout page on a desk with a small robot beside it, natural light
scenes.speaker: Arjun

scenes.narration: A robot that practises in a simulation, then wakes up already walking. Follow for more robots learning to walk.
